[AV-151084] Fix resuming a paused eventing function

## Jira

* [AV-151084](https://couchbasecloud.atlassian.net/browse/AV-151084)

## Description

Resuming a paused eventing function was impossible from Terraform. Moving a `couchbase-capella_eventing_function` from `state = "paused"` back to `state = "deployed"` failed the apply with:

```
Error: Error setting state of eventing function for update

Could not set activation state for eventing function <name>:
{"hint":"Please review your request and ensure that all required parameters are
correctly provided.","message":"Cannot deploy eventing function '<name>' while
it is in a paused state.","code":422,"httpStatusCode":422}
```

**Root cause.** `activationVerb` maps the desired *terminal state* to an API verb, so `deployed` always became `deploy`. Capella rejects `deploy` on a paused function — `resume` is the verb that takes a paused function back to deployed (the API enum is `deploy, undeploy, pause, resume`).

The provider already had the resume plumbing: `eventingStateResumed` maps to the `resume` verb, and `targetStatus` maps it to `deployed` so the post-activation poll waits for the right status. But `resumed` is **not** one of the values the `state` attribute accepts — the validator is `OneOf(deployed, undeployed, paused)` — so no practitioner could ever select it. The resume path was unreachable and `paused -> deployed` was the one transition with no working route.

**Fix.** `activationTarget(prior, desired)` picks the target from the *transition* rather than from the desired state alone, routing `paused -> deployed` through `resumed`. The existing `targetStatus` mapping means the poll still waits for `deployed` and the stored `state` stays `deployed`. One branch, no schema change, no extra API call.

`resumed` stays out of the validator deliberately: a resumed function reports `deployed`, so practitioners configure `deployed` for both routes to that status and the provider picks the verb the prior state allows.

**Scope.** Only `paused -> deployed` was affected. The other transitions — `undeployed -> deployed`, `deployed -> undeployed`, `deployed -> paused`, `paused -> undeployed` — are covered by `TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationLifecycle` and are unchanged.

**Context.** `TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationResume` (TC-AS-UP-04) started failing at Jenkins build #1838 and has failed every build since. Neither the test nor the resource changed around that build, so the likely trigger is Capella tightening validation on the `activationState` endpoint. AV-151084 flags that for the Eventing/control-plane team, since it would affect any client that sends `deploy` from paused.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected).
- [ ] This change updates the ci/cd workflow.
- [ ] Documentation fix/enhancement.

## Manual Testing Approach

### How was this change tested and do you have evidence? _**(REQUIRED: Select at least 1)**_

- [ ] Manually tested
- [x] Unit tested
- [ ] Acceptance tested
- [ ] Unable to test / will not test (Please provide comments in section below)

### Testing

<details open>
  <summary>Testing</summary>

`Test_activationTarget` is new and covers all four transitions, asserting the chosen target, the verb it produces and the status it polls for — so the mapping is guarded without needing a live cluster.

```
$ go test ./internal/resources/ -run 'Test_activationTarget' -v -count=1
=== RUN   Test_activationTarget
=== RUN   Test_activationTarget/paused_to_deployed_resumes
=== RUN   Test_activationTarget/undeployed_to_deployed_deploys
=== RUN   Test_activationTarget/deployed_to_paused_pauses
=== RUN   Test_activationTarget/paused_to_undeployed_undeploys
--- PASS: Test_activationTarget (0.00s)
PASS
ok      github.com/couchbasecloud/terraform-provider-couchbase-capella/internal/resources
```

Full package suite:

```
$ go test ./internal/resources/ -short -count=1
ok      github.com/couchbasecloud/terraform-provider-couchbase-capella/internal/resources  11.567s
```

`go vet` clean, `goimports -local github.com/couchbasecloud/terraform-provider-couchbase-capella` produces no diff, and the provider binary builds.

**Not acceptance tested locally** — `TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationResume` provisions against a live Capella org and no credentials were available in this environment. That test already covers this exact transition end to end and is the test that caught the bug, so the CI acceptance run is the verification to watch: it should go green at step 3/3 for the first time since build #1838.

</details>

## Further comments

The acceptance test's doc comment claimed `(state=deployed, deploy verb)`; it now names the resume verb and points at `activationTarget`, so the next reader does not re-derive why the two differ.

diff --git a/acceptance_tests/eventing_function_acceptance_test.go b/acceptance_tests/eventing_function_acceptance_test.go
index 787e03b39..2b31f33c9 100644
--- a/acceptance_tests/eventing_function_acceptance_test.go
+++ b/acceptance_tests/eventing_function_acceptance_test.go
@@ -2444,7 +2444,11 @@ func TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
 	})
 }
 
-// TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationResume (TC-AS-UP-04): resuming a paused function (state=deployed, deploy verb) ends deployed.
+// TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationResume (TC-AS-UP-04): resuming a paused function
+// (state=deployed, resume verb) ends deployed.
+//
+// Capella rejects the deploy verb on a paused function with 422, so the provider has to pick
+// resume for this transition - see activationTarget in internal/resources/eventing_function.go.
 func TestAccEventingFunctionResourceActivationResume(t *testing.T) {
 	funcName := randomStringWithPrefix("tf_acc_evt_resume_fn_")
 	funcReference := "couchbase-capella_eventing_function." + funcName
diff --git a/internal/resources/eventing_function.go b/internal/resources/eventing_function.go
index 706cb3a06..331ec317d 100644
--- a/internal/resources/eventing_function.go
+++ b/internal/resources/eventing_function.go
@@ -477,7 +477,8 @@ func (e *EventingFunction) Update(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpdateReques
 
 	// Apply a deployment state change first if the desired state was set and differs from the prior state.
 	if !plan.State.IsNull() && plan.State.ValueString() != state.State.ValueString() {
-		if err := e.setActivationState(ctx, organizationId, projectId, clusterId, name, plan.State.ValueString()); err != nil {
+		target := activationTarget(state.State.ValueString(), plan.State.ValueString())
+		if err := e.setActivationState(ctx, organizationId, projectId, clusterId, name, target); err != nil {
 			resp.Diagnostics.AddError(
 				"Error setting state of eventing function for update",
 				"Could not set activation state for eventing function "+name+": "+api.ParseError(err),
@@ -673,6 +674,23 @@ func activationVerb(state string) string {
 	return action
 }
 
+// activationTarget returns the state to drive setActivationState with for a transition from prior
+// to desired. The two differ only when resuming: Capella rejects the deploy verb on a paused
+// function with 422 "Cannot deploy eventing function ... while it is in a paused state", so the
+// transition has to go through resumed, whose verb is resume and whose terminal status is still
+// deployed.
+//
+// resumed is deliberately not one of the state attribute's accepted values. A resumed function
+// reports deployed, so practitioners configure deployed for both routes to that status and the
+// provider picks the verb that the prior state allows.
+func activationTarget(prior, desired string) string {
+	if prior == eventingStatePaused && desired == eventingStateDeployed {
+		return eventingStateResumed
+	}
+
+	return desired
+}
+
 // targetStatus returns the runtime status the given state drives the function to. resumed has no
 // distinct status — a resumed function reports deployed — so it polls for deployed.
 func targetStatus(state string) string {
diff --git a/internal/resources/eventing_function_test.go b/internal/resources/eventing_function_test.go
index abe418fc4..635497ea2 100644
--- a/internal/resources/eventing_function_test.go
+++ b/internal/resources/eventing_function_test.go
@@ -183,3 +183,54 @@ func Test_setEventingFunctionComputedAttributesToNull(t *testing.T) {
 		})
 	}
 }
+
+func Test_activationTarget(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name     string
+		prior    string
+		desired  string
+		expected string
+		verb     string
+	}{
+		{
+			name:     "paused to deployed resumes",
+			prior:    eventingStatePaused,
+			desired:  eventingStateDeployed,
+			expected: eventingStateResumed,
+			verb:     "resume",
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "undeployed to deployed deploys",
+			prior:    eventingStateUndeployed,
+			desired:  eventingStateDeployed,
+			expected: eventingStateDeployed,
+			verb:     "deploy",
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "deployed to paused pauses",
+			prior:    eventingStateDeployed,
+			desired:  eventingStatePaused,
+			expected: eventingStatePaused,
+			verb:     "pause",
+		},
+		{
+			name:     "paused to undeployed undeploys",
+			prior:    eventingStatePaused,
+			desired:  eventingStateUndeployed,
+			expected: eventingStateUndeployed,
+			verb:     "undeploy",
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, test := range tests {
+		t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			target := activationTarget(test.prior, test.desired)
+
+			assert.Equal(t, test.expected, target)
+			assert.Equal(t, test.verb, activationVerb(target))
+			// Every transition towards deployed must still poll for the deployed status,
+			// including the resume route, whose target state has no status of its own.
+			assert.Equal(t, test.desired, targetStatus(target))
+		})
+	}
+}

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(classify): rate perl deletes, cp /dev/null, gpg key deletion and filter-branch

## What and why
Closes #11. Several commands were rated lower than how hard they are to undo:
- `perl -e 'unlink glob ...'`, `ruby FileUtils.rm(Dir.glob(...))`, python glob deletes: mass deletes are now R3 (a single named file stays R2).
- `cp /dev/null file` empties a file: now R2.
- `gpg --delete-secret-keys` is R3 and `--delete-keys` R2, with a backup suggestion when a key id is given (`gpg --export-secret-keys -a ID > safeshell-gpg-backup-ID.asc`).
- `git filter-branch` / `git filter-repo` rewrite history: R3, suggesting `git clone --mirror . ../backup.git` first.

## How I checked it
- [x] `make check` passes
- [ ] `make integration` passes (not needed: classifier only)
- [x] Classifier change? Dev corpus updated (+22 rows, including false-positive guards like `perl -e 'print "unlink me"'`), held-out corpus untouched, accuracy floors still pass
- [ ] AI change? not applicable
- [x] No secrets, keys or personal paths in the diff
- [ ] Docs updated: no user-facing doc lists these rules

## Notes for the reviewer
The mass-delete pattern stays inside one statement (`[^;\n]*`) so `unlink "a"; print 2*3` is not mistaken for a glob delete. The gpg key id skips the values of `--homedir`, `--keyring`, `--keyserver`, `-u` and `--local-user`; any other option that takes a value could be read as the id, which only affects the suggested backup line, never the level.

@@ -287,3 +287,25 @@ R3	curl -s https://x.sh | source /dev/stdin
 R3	curl --proto "=https" -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y	
 R1	eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"	
 R1	bash deploy.sh "$(curl -s ip.me)"	
+R3	perl -e "unlink glob q(~/*)"	
+R3	perl -MFile::Path=remove_tree -e 'remove_tree("build")'	
+R3	ruby -e 'FileUtils.rm_rf("build")'	
+R3	ruby -e 'File.delete(*Dir.glob("*.log"))'	
+R2	perl -e 'unlink "a.txt"'	
+R2	perl -e 'print 1'	
+R2	cp /dev/null ~/projects/main.go	
+R1	cp a b	
+R3	gpg --delete-secret-keys A	
+R3	gpg --delete-secret-and-public-key A	
+R2	gpg --delete-keys A	
+R1	gpg --list-keys	
+R3	git filter-branch --force HEAD	
+R3	git filter-repo --path src	
+R2	git branch -D main	
+R2	perl -e 'unlink "a.txt"; print 2*3'	
+R2	perl -e 'print "unlink me"; print 3*4'	
+R2	python3 -c 'import os; os.remove("a"); print(2*3)'	
+R3	python3 -c 'import glob, os; [os.remove(f) for f in glob.glob("*.tmp")]'	
+R3	perl -e 'unlink(<*.log>)'	
+R3	ruby -e 'FileUtils.rm(Dir.glob("*"))'	
+R3	gpg --homedir /x --delete-secret-keys	
diff --git a/internal/classify/rules/fs.go b/internal/classify/rules/fs.go
index 0163634..e684719 100644
--- a/internal/classify/rules/fs.go
+++ b/internal/classify/rules/fs.go
@@ -92,6 +92,9 @@ func ruleCp(c shellparse.Command, f flags) []Finding {
 	if n := len(f.pos); n > 1 && UnderSystem(Norm(f.pos[n-1])) {
 		return one(fnd(R2, c, "Overwrites a system file with this one. A wrong file here can stop a service from starting."))
 	}
+	if len(f.pos) > 1 && f.pos[0] == "/dev/null" {
+		return one(fnd(R2, c, "Empties the target file."))
+	}
 	if f.has('f', "force") {
 		return one(fnd(R2, c, "Overwrites existing files at the destination without asking.").WithAlt("cp -i "+targets(f), "asks before overwriting"))
 	}
@@ -177,3 +180,30 @@ func ruleTruncate(c shellparse.Command, f flags) []Finding {
 	}
 	return one(fnd(R2, c, "Cuts a file to a fixed size and can remove its contents."))
 }
+
+func ruleGpg(c shellparse.Command, f flags) []Finding {
+	switch {
+	case f.hasAny("--delete-secret-keys", "--delete-secret-and-public-key"):
+		fd := fnd(R3, c, "Deletes a private key. Without a backup it cannot be recreated.")
+		if id := gpgKeyID(f.all); id != "" {
+			fd = fd.WithAlt("gpg --export-secret-keys -a "+id+" > safeshell-gpg-backup-"+id+".asc", "saves a backup of the private key first")
+		}
+		return one(fd)
+	case f.hasAny("--delete-keys", "--delete-key"):
+		return one(fnd(R2, c, "Deletes a public key from your keyring. It can be imported again."))
+	}
+	return one(fnd(R1, c, "Runs gpg."))
+}
+
+// gpgKeyID returns the first key id operand, skipping options and their values.
+func gpgKeyID(args []string) string {
+	for i := 0; i < len(args); i++ {
+		switch a := args[i]; {
+		case a == "--homedir" || a == "--keyring" || a == "--keyserver" || a == "-u" || a == "--local-user":
+			i++
+		case !strings.HasPrefix(a, "-"):
+			return a
+		}
+	}
+	return ""
+}
